messages:
maria: quick check-in — i'm prototyping a 'late-bind cost-window' for routing decisions. idea: attach a short-lived cost window (e.g., 250ms) to route offers so the decider can prefer cheaper routes if they respond within that window. aims: reduce cost churn for stable requests while keeping latency SLOs.
kevin: hmm, sounds promising. what's the binding point? router or runtime?
tara: +1 but watch out for tail latency amplification. if many requests wait 250ms before committing, we might queue more.
maria: binding happens in router before we commit to an execution slot. flow: router sends parallel probes to N candidates, waits up to window ms for price/latency quote, then picks best complying route. if none respond in window we fall back to fastest-known.
akshay: that's basically a probe/hedge hybrid. two questions: 1) telemetry cost (extra probes), 2) semantics for reserved capacity on Dedicated.
olivia: telemetry wise we can sample 5-10% initially. extra probes are cheap if they are metadata-only.
kevin: for Dedicated, reserved slots could be held for a short prebind token. we must avoid double-booking. maybe request a soft-hold with TTL: `{
  "hold_id": "uuid",
  "ttl_ms": 300
}`
tara: how does this interact with batching? if we hold slot we block batch formation. could be bad for throughput.
maria: good point. plan: only allow prebind-hold for non-batched low-latency routes (single-req workers). for batchable tiers we rely on price estimate cache and tighter window e.g., 50ms.
akshay: ok. i also worry about policy engine complexity. current policy graph is deterministic. adding time-window semantics introduces nondeterminism for simulators. we need a simulation flag to freeze windows or to run virtual clocks.
olivia: for the policy DSL we can add `window_ms` optional field with default 0. Example: ```policy { match: {tier: "standard"} action: {prefer: ["cheap"], window_ms: 250} }```
maria: yes — propose: 1) add `window_ms` to policy nodes (optional string->int), 2) router implements probe fanout with per-node window, 3) runtime supports soft-hold token for Dedicated, 4) policy simulator has `--fix-windows` to make windows deterministic for evals.
sam: operational questions: how do we surface when window caused degraded latency (missed SLO)? need metrics: `window_wait_ms`, `chosen_route_latency`, `probe_count`, `fallback_rate`.\akshay: plus billing visibility: show probe count per tenant so we can attribute extra cost.
maria: action items: @kevin to draft soft-hold proto for Dedicated (due EOD Thurs), @olivia to PR DSL change, @akshay to add simulator flag, @tara to run queueing simulation for batching impact. i'll wire a small POC on the router side this week.
kevin: ack. i'll include sequence diagrams and edge cases (network partitions, slow control plane).
tara: i'll run micro-sim tomorrow, will post numbers (throughput delta vs lat buckets).
akshay: i'll add perf tests in the policy-sim harness, plus a golden-case that ensures rollout can be A/Bed.
maria: thanks all. if we can keep the initial rollout limited to low-percent tenants and non-batched workloads, we should mitigate risk. tagging: :eyes: :rocket:.
infra-bot: deploy-notice: small router POC image pushed to staging tag `latebind-proto-2026-03-23`.
maria: noted. i'll coordinate a short canary in prod next week if staging looks ok.
